ev.q: CDC compared national estimates of sepsis-related mortality based on death certificates using the CDC WONDER database
was 15% to 140% higher than annual estimates generated using death certificates (multiple causes)
the annual number of all reported sepsis-related deaths increased 31%, from 139,086 in 1999 to 182,242 in 2014
a total of 2,470,666 decedents (6% of all deaths) had sepsis listed among the causes of death
Among decedents, approximately 49% were aged 65–84 years, 26% were aged ≥85 years
for 22% of these decedents, sepsis was listed as the underlying cause of death
was 15% to 140% higher than annual estimates generated using death certificates (multiple causes)
Multiple cause-of-death mortality files maintained in the CDC WONDER database were reviewed to analyze deaths

methods_quotes.q: Death certificate data were obtained from multiple cause-of-death records of the National Vital Statistics System, using CDC’s WONDER database
defined as deaths with diagnoses corresponding to International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) diagnosis codes A40
The annual sepsis mortality estimates based on death certificates from the WONDER database were then compared with the previously published annual estimates
